name: Buenos Aires
tagline: European Elegance at South American Prices
description: Buenos Aires is the Paris of South America — grand architecture, world-class steak and wine, and a cultural scene that rivals any global capital. Argentina's economic volatility means the dollar stretches extraordinarily far, making it possible to live a genuinely luxurious life on a modest FIRE budget, though currency fluctuations add an element of unpredictability.

quickFacts.visa: Rentista Visa (requires proof of stable income ~$1,500/mo from abroad; renewable annually) or Pensionado Visa for retirees
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate — safe in Palermo, Recoleta, Belgrano; pickpocketing common in tourist areas
quickFacts.climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, mild winters, four distinct seasons
quickFacts.currency: Argentine Peso (ARS) — significant parallel exchange rate ('blue dollar') benefits foreigners

housing.description: Furnished monoambiente/studio in a characterful non-prime barrio (Almagro, Boedo, Villa Crespo)

dining.description: Mostly home cooking; empanadas, a neighborhood parrilla, or a menú del día a few times a week

healthcare.description: Entry local prepaga (OSDE 210). Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees should budget more.

entertainment.description: Free parks/museum days, cheap milongas, a gym, a fútbol match

1M.lifestyle: A furnished monoambiente in a characterful non-prime barrio like Almagro, Boedo, or Villa Crespo, walkable to cafés and the subte. Most meals are cooked at home, with empanadas, a neighborhood parrilla, or a menú del día a few times a week, and getting around runs on the SUBE with the occasional Uber. Health cover is an entry OSDE prepaga, enough for private clinics. Free parks, museum days, cheap milongas, and a fútbol match fill the weeks. Buenos Aires no longer feels bargain-cheap in dollars now that the peso has firmed, but this is a frugal, culturally rich life.

housing.description: Furnished 1BR in a good-but-not-prime barrio (Colegiales, Caballito) or a compact Palermo studio

dining.description: Out a few times a week, mid-range plus the occasional parrilla dinner with wine

2M.lifestyle: A furnished one-bedroom in a good-but-unpretentious barrio like Colegiales, Caballito, or the Villa Crespo edge, or a compact Palermo studio. Dining out a few times a week — mid-range spots and the occasional parrilla dinner with a bottle of Malbec — becomes routine, and comprehensive OSDE 310 cover removes the entry-plan limits. Transport mixes the subte with regular Uber, and the budget stretches to a gym, theatre, wine bars, and an active nightlife. Comfortable and unhurried in one of the continent's great walking cities.

housing.description: Comfortable furnished 1BR in prime Palermo or Recoleta

dining.description: Frequent mid-range tables plus regular steakhouse dinners with good wine

healthcare.description: Strong upper-mid local prepaga (OSDE 410) with broad access to the top private clinics

entertainment.description: Theatre, concerts, the occasional Teatro Colón seat, a premium gym

3M.lifestyle: A comfortable furnished one-bedroom in prime Palermo or Recoleta, on a leafy street near the best cafés and restaurants. Dining out is frequent — mid-range tables plus regular steakhouse dinners with good wine — and health cover steps up to a strong OSDE 410 plan. Nights out mean theatre, concerts, the occasional Teatro Colón seat, and a premium gym, with Uber and remis covering transport. This is an affluent porteño life, well above what most locals experience, in Buenos Aires's most desirable neighborhoods.

dining.description: Near-weekly fine dining and premium parrillas

healthcare.description: OSDE flagship tier (450/510-level) with an international add-on

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeper a few days a week (min ~ARS 3,600/hr, Jun-2026)

5M.lifestyle: A large luxury apartment in Puerto Madero or top Palermo/Recoleta, with a housekeeper coming a few days a week. Fine dining and premium parrillas are near-weekly, health cover is the OSDE flagship tier plus an international add-on, and transport is premium ride-hailing and car service. The discretionary budget funds opera, polo, wine-club membership, a personal trainer, and a standing travel fund. Buenos Aires's cultural depth — arts, tango, gastronomy — makes this an unusually rich version of upper-tier living.

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining, Don Julio-tier and the closed-door circuit

healthcare.description: International concierge cover WITH medical evacuation (worldwide-excl-US expat plan, priced for 45–55); plans like this are priced the same wherever you're based

entertainment.description: Teatro Colón boxes, polo, VIP nightlife, premium memberships

luxuryExtras.description: Art and wine collecting, personal shopper, club/polo memberships, first/business travel fund, uncapped discretionary

10M.lifestyle: A best-address residence — a Puerto Madero tower or a grand Recoleta apartment — with a full-time housekeeper and cook. Dining is near-daily at the city's finest tables, from Don Julio to the closed-door circuit, and healthcare shifts to an international concierge plan with worldwide coverage and medical evacuation. A private driver and premium car handle transport, and the uncapped discretionary budget runs to Teatro Colón boxes, polo, art and wine collecting, and first-class travel. This is Buenos Aires at its most opulent — a trophy address, resident staff, and the full sweep of the city's grand cultural life.
